topic: `sign_v1` Allows Malicious Instructions on Accounts Without Proper Restrictions [Swig / Rust]
post_text:
1/ Swig protocol allows malicious instructions on restricted accounts via sign_v1. A user with TokenLimit can transfer authority without balance changes, bypassing access controls entirely. [KB: SS-03699]

2/ The instruction checks permissions only when balances shift. It ignores actions like SetAuthority that modify control but leave token amounts untouched. This logic flaw permits unauthorized ownership transfers.

3/ An attacker with minimal TokenLimit can execute arbitrary CPIs on any account type. Stake accounts and other state structures face similar risks where control changes do not trigger permission checks.

4/ The proof of concept confirms second_authority gains full control over a token account despite holding only a limited transfer allowance. Ownership transfers succeed because the balance remains constant.

5/ Remediation requires restricting instruction types per account role. Token accounts must permit only Transfer, Burn, and Mint operations. No other actions should execute without explicit approval.

6/ Implement strict invariant checks before CPI execution. Verify that every allowed instruction matches the assigned authority configuration for that specific account type.

7/ SanadSquad covers the whole attack surface, not just the contract. Our Web3 Security audits address these access control gaps across EVM and Solana environments.
